name: Battle of Thermopylae

phases.title: The Greeks hold the middle gate
phases.text: Leonidas camped at the narrowest part of the pass, where the Phocians had built a wall, and posted 1,000 Phocians on the heights above. The Persian army came up across the Malian Gulf.

phases.title: Xerxes's archers shoot first
phases.text: On the first day Xerxes ordered 5,000 archers to shoot a barrage of arrows. They shot from at least 100 yards away, and the Greeks' wooden shields and bronze helmets deflected the arrows.

phases.title: The Medes attack the Greek line
phases.text: Xerxes sent 10,000 Medes and Cissians forward, and the Persians launched a frontal assault in waves of about 10,000 men. The Greeks fought in front of the Phocian wall, at the narrowest part of the pass.

phases.title: The Immortals fare no better
phases.text: Xerxes threw the Immortals into a second assault the same day, and they made no headway. On the second day the Persian infantry again attacked the pass without success.

phases.title: Xerxes withdraws to his camp
phases.text: Xerxes stopped the assault and withdrew to his camp, as the Persians had had no more success than on the first day.

phases.title: Ephialtes shows the mountain path
phases.text: A Trachinian named Ephialtes told Xerxes of the mountain path around Thermopylae. Hydarnes set out that evening with the Immortals to encircle the Greeks.

phases.title: The Phocians see the Persian column
phases.text: The Phocians guarding the path became aware of the outflanking Persian column. They retreated to a nearby hill to make their stand, assuming the Persians had come to attack them.

phases.title: The Persians bypass the Phocians
phases.text: Not wishing to be delayed, the Persians merely shot a volley of arrows at the Phocians. They then went on past them with the encirclement of the main Greek force.

phases.title: Leonidas lets his allies leave
phases.text: Learning that his army had been encircled, Leonidas told his allies that they could leave if they wanted to. Many did, and around 2,000 soldiers stayed behind.

phases.title: The Greeks sally from the wall
phases.text: A Persian force of 10,000 light infantry and cavalry charged the front of the Greek formation. The Spartans and Thespians marched out from the wall to meet it in the wider part of the pass. Leonidas was killed.

phases.title: The Greeks withdraw to the hill
phases.text: As the Immortals approached, the Greeks withdrew from the wall and took a stand on a hill behind it. The Spartans and Thespians moved there together.

phases.title: The Thebans surrender
phases.text: The Thebans moved away from their companions and advanced towards the Persians with their hands upraised. A few were killed before their surrender was accepted.

phases.title: The last stand on the hill
phases.text: Xerxes had part of the wall torn down and the hill surrounded, and the Persians shot arrows until every last Greek was dead.

note: The Malian Gulf lay on the north side of the road and steep hills on the other, so north is drawn at the top. The accounts do not say which Greek contingent stood where along the line, so the Greek blocks are placed by judgement, and the arrows show only that the Persians attacked the Greek line. The Persians are drawn coming from the east, which the account does not state. The marsh the Phocians made, and the hill to which the Phocians retreated, are not drawn because the accounts do not place them. Herodotus names the Immortals as the men sent along the path; Diodorus gives Hydarnes a force of 20,000, and the account says it is unclear who the men were.
